title: Resolving the two ties of the motor-level test with a finer dose grid (SIMULATED)
status: registered before any of the finer dose levels was run
relation_to_parent: MR5 failed as registered (chip later than motor output in 3 families, tied in 2, earlier in 0; 4 needed). That outcome stands. This test does not re-score MR5; it asks a new question: which comes first inside the two dose steps where the parent's grid could not tell.
seen_before_registration: all parent results; the two tied families and their coarse onsets: excitability_block (threshold_scale 1.4, dose 0.4, for both motor output and the chip; at 1.2 the chip's |delta log2 mfr| was 0.14 and the motor disruption 0.41) and gaba_potentiate (gaba_scale 2.0, dose 1.0, for both; at 1.5 the chip's |delta| was 0.49 and the motor disruption 0.36)

design.model_and_readouts: exactly the parent's: MaleCNS model, chip array readouts by the replication's code, motor readouts and motor disruption by fly.motor
design.seeds: spontaneous 500-502 and behaviour 600-607, the parent's, so the untreated reference is unchanged
design.references: chip deltas against the replication's vehicle (malecns_conditions_SIMULATED.csv); motor disruption against the parent's vehicle (malecns_motor_SIMULATED.csv)
design.onset_rule: first dose, in the parent's levels below the tie step followed by the fine levels and the tied level, at which motor disruption >= 0.5 (motor) or |delta log2 mfr| >= 0.5 (chip)
design.resolution: chip later if the motor onset is the lower dose, chip earlier if the chip onset is lower, still tied if equal

TB0_tied_levels_reproduce.statement: Re-running the two tied levels with the same seeds gives the parent's values
TB0_tied_levels_reproduce.test: max |difference| in |delta log2 mfr| and motor disruption <= 1e-9

TB1_both_ties_resolve_chip_later.statement: Inside both tie steps, motor output fails before the chip detects
TB1_both_ties_resolve_chip_later.test: both tied families resolve to chip later

reporting: Each family's resolution (chip later, chip earlier, still tied) and both predictions, whichever way they fall, reported beside the parent's MR5, not in place of it.
